text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwean government will have to wait until the middle of next year for financial support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for its economic reform programme, during which time the IMF will be looking at how the government moves to reduce its budget deficit.

- Zimbabwean doctors on Monday disputed the salary scales for medical staff given on Sunday by acting public service, labour and social welfare minister Nathan Shamuyarira, saying his figures were "ridiculous".

- Zimbabwe riot police on Monday used teargas and batons to disperse about 200 demonstrators who had gathered at the Harare magistrates court for a protest march over the health crisis prevailing in the southern African country after junior doctors and nurses went on strike three weeks ago demanding higher wages and better working conditions.
